Legal_Issue: Whether allegations about refusal to settle and procedural history are permissible in pleadings
Application_Facts: Rothmans included allegations about Imperial's refusal to negotiate settlement and procedural history in their Statement of Defence; Imperial moved to strike those parts
Decision_Outcome: Second and last sentences of paragraph five remain; third and fourth sentences struck
Remedy_Requested: Imperial requested striking irrelevant portions of Rothmans' Statement of Defence
Court_Ruling: Parts of the pleading not relevant to patent validity or infringement were struck
Defendant_Behavior: Rothmans included allegations regarding settlement refusal and procedural matters
Grounds_for_Claim: Pleadings must be relevant to patent validity and infringement
Legal_Standard: Pleadings must be relevant to the lis and directly connected to the issues in dispute
Assessment_Factor: Relevance of allegations to core issues of patent validity and infringement
Procedural_Issue: Allegations about consolidation and settlement negotiations in pleadings
Application_Basis: Rules of pleading in patent disputes
Relief_Sought: Striking improper allegations from the Statement of Defence
Governing_Rule: Pleadings must be relevant to the issues of patent validity and infringement
Evidentiary_Deficiency: Allegations of motive and procedural conduct not supported by proper evidentiary context in pleadings
Outcome: Partial success for Imperial—irrelevant allegations struck
Cause_Description: Imperial sought declaration of patent invalidity or non-infringement after threat of legal action from Rothmans
Decision_Rationale: Allegations about refusal to settle are not part of the lis unless directly connected to validity or infringement
Legal_Standard_Applied: Relevance and connection of pleadings to core legal issues in patent disputes

Legal_Issue: Whether the immigration officer's decision was unreasonable due to failure to consider significant evidence
Application_Facts: Ms. Ratnarajah's application cited risks for Tamils returning to Sri Lanka; UNHCR reports indicated serious risks
Decision_Outcome: H&C application dismissed by officer
Court_Ruling: Judicial review granted; decision remanded for reconsideration by another officer
Claimant_Status: Applicant for humanitarian and compassionate relief
Defendant_Behavior: Immigration officer dismissed application without addressing specific UNHCR reports
Grounds_for_Claim: Overlooked evidence of risk to Tamils in Sri Lanka
Legal_Standard: A decision is unreasonable if it fails to consider significant evidence or explain dismissal of contradictory evidence
Assessment_Factor: Country conditions in Sri Lanka, particularly for Tamils
Procedural_Issue: Judicial review of administrative decision
Evidence_Used: UNHCR reports indicating risks for Tamils in Sri Lanka
Application_Basis: Humanitarian and compassionate grounds based on risk upon return
Evidence_Assessed: General improvements in Sri Lanka (considered); UNHCR reports on Tamil persecution (not adequately addressed)
Governing_Rule: A decision is unreasonable if it fails to consider significant evidence or explain why contradictory evidence was dismissed
Evidentiary_Deficiency: Failure to address specific UNHCR reports
Harm_Assessment: Risk of harm to Ms. Ratnarajah as a Tamil returning to Sri Lanka
Cause_Description: Ms. Ratnarajah's H&C application was dismissed despite evidence suggesting hardship in returning to Sri Lanka
Evidence_Handling: Officer failed to properly assess or explain dismissal of UNHCR reports
Evidence_Assessment: Insufficient; key evidence not meaningfully considered
Decision_Rationale: Reliance on general country conditions without addressing individualized risks
Evidentiary_Issues: Failure to consider or reconcile contradictory evidence from UNHCR
